title: Coral and the Veil
premise: Edmund Amberdale, a royal food-taster slowly poisoning himself toward immunity, has never left the valley where magic cannot follow — until Coral, tonight's dinner date, turns out to be named in a century-old book of prophecies as the one who will reforge the broken covenant between realms. When dragon-fire begins to gutter out and the veil between worlds starts failing, Coral is pulled through it into a realm that has been waiting for her, while Edmund must do the unthinkable: leave the only safe ground he's ever known. Together they discover the covenant was broken deliberately by those who profit from the realms' division, and that reforging it demands a life freely given. In the end, Edmund offers his poisoned, half-immortal body as the new anchor for the covenant; Coral, refusing to let him die alone, binds herself beside him, and the two survive transformed — no longer quite of either realm, but finally belonging to each other.
about_author: Vesper Dravenmoor is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing medieval covenant documents and oath-books before turning to fiction. They write fantasy about people bound by duty they never chose, from a house at the edge of a valley much like Edmund's.

chapters.title: The Taster's Tongue
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. We meet him mid-service, sipping arsenic-laced wine with practiced calm, counting the dishes between him and full immunity — and freedom to leave the valley where magic cannot follow. That evening he meets Coral for a first date at a riverside tavern. Emotional beat: longing disguised as routine; the quiet ache of a man whose survival is also his cage.

chapters.title: A Name in Old Ink
chapters.summary: Coral's POV, then Edmund's. Coral, an antiquarian bookbinder, recognizes her own name and tonight's date inscribed in a prophecy book written a century ago. She laughs it off over dinner — until the candle flames bend sideways and the veil tears open above their table. Emotional beat: wonder curdling into terror as the impossible chooses her.

chapters.title: Through the Veil
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. She is pulled through into the other realm, landing in a dying forest where dragon-fire gutters in stone braziers and hollow-eyed wardens insist she is 'the Reforger.' She learns the covenant binding the realms was broken a hundred years ago, and the veil is now failing. Emotional beat: disorientation hardening into resolve; she will not be a pawn.

chapters.title: The Man Who Crossed
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Leaving the valley means leaving behind his immunity's protection — every poison in his blood becomes volatile outside. He crosses anyway, guided by a warden deserter named Brack who knows what breaking the covenant cost. Emotional beat: fear overcome by something larger than self-preservation; the taster choosing risk over safety for the first time.

chapters.title: What the Wardens Buried
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. Coral discovers the covenant wasn't broken by accident: the wardens' council shattered it deliberately, feeding on the veil's decay to extend their own lives. The last dragon, Ashveil, confirms it in a voice like cooling embers. Emotional beat: righteous fury; justice revealed as something the law itself cannot provide.

chapters.title: The Guttering Flame
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. With days left before the last dragon-fire dies and both realms collapse into each other, Coral attempts the reforging rite alone — and fails, learning it requires a willing mortal anchor, not a chosen one. Meanwhile Edmund reaches the forest, poisoned and shaking. Emotional beat: despair and the crushing weight of being 'the one' without the power to be it.

chapters.title: Poison as Prayer
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Edmund realizes his half-immortal body — saturated with a hundred toxins, alive when nothing should live — is exactly the anchor the rite needs. He volunteers without telling Coral the price. Brack, once a covenant-breaker himself, chooses to stand witness and betray the council. Emotional beat: sacrifice offered quietly, love expressed as willingness.

chapters.title: The Council's Teeth
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. The wardens' council captures them, intending to kill Edmund and force Coral to renew their parasitic pact instead. In the cells beneath the council hall, Coral and Edmund finally speak honestly — about cages, belonging, and why each crossed a world for the other. Emotional beat: intimacy forged in captivity; the decision to fight together.

chapters.title: Ashveil Rises
chapters.summary: Both POVs interwoven. Ashveil breaks free, burning the council hall as Brack opens the cells. Amid the chaos, Coral and Edmund reach the heartfire and begin the rite — Edmund offering his poisoned body, Coral seizing his hand and binding herself alongside him so neither anchors alone. Emotional beat: climax; fury, fire, and defiance answered by mutual choice.

chapters.title: Two Names, One Covenant
chapters.summary: Coral's POV, closing with Edmund's. The covenant reforges around them both; they survive, changed — able to walk both realms but fully at home in neither, except together. The wardens fall, Brack carries word home, and Ashveil's flame steadies. Back in the valley, they finish the date the veil interrupted. Emotional beat: resolution; belonging redefined not as a place, but as a person.
